title: Penalty for giving or asking for advice
question: You ask your playing partner, 'Which club should I use for this shot?' What happens according to the rules?

choices.text: Both you and your partner get 1 penalty stroke.

explanation: If you ask for or receive advice like club selection during a round, you get a 2-stroke penalty.

juniorVersion.title: What happens if you ask your friend which club to use?
juniorVersion.question: You say to your friend, 'Which club should I use for this shot?' What does the rule say will happen?

choices.text: You get 2 extra shots added to your score.
Your friend gets 2 extra shots added to their score.
You and your friend each get 1 extra shot added.

juniorVersion.explanation: The rules say you must choose your club on your own. If you ask your friend which club to use, you get 2 shots added to your score.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: Extra shots added to your score if you break a rule.
When someone tells you what to do, like which club to use.

juniorVersion.teachingTip: Explain that golf is about making choices for yourself. Remind children not to ask or tell friends what club to use during a round.
likelyMisconceptions: Children may think it's okay to ask friends for help during play.
They might believe both players are penalised.
